historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle revenue: between the 5-year (2.9%, FY2020-25) and 10-year (5.3%, FY2015-25) revenue CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is NEGATIVE (-2.4% 5yr) while revenue and EPS CAGRs are positive: EXPD returns more than it earns via buybacks (TTM 901m repurchased vs 794m owner FCF), so book value is not a growth anchor for this company. The 3-year CAGRs on every line are distorted by the FY2021-22 freight-rate super-cycle (revenue 17.1bn in FY2022 vs 9.3bn in FY2023) and are not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for the FCF CAGRs: FY2020 523.9 (607.4 reported - 73.1 SBC incl. equity taxes - 10.4 interest), FY2022 1,933.6 (2,042.9 - 83.7 - 25.6), FY2025 838.1 (953.4 - 79.6 - 35.7). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.5pp of each other: SBC is ~0.7% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow. Per-share figures compound ~4-5pp faster than the aggregates because the count fell from 170.9m (FY2020) to 130.4m; that is the buyback mechanism, not operating growth, and the model does not credit it.

scenario_narratives.base: The two 2025-26 tailwinds -- AI-hyperscaler server airfreight needing upper-deck freighter capacity, and tariff/IEEPA-driven customs complexity lifting the highest-margin brokerage line -- carry the Q2-2026 run-rate through H2-2026, then fade through 2027 as freighter capacity is added, tariff refund work runs off and airfreight yields normalise (year 2 -3%). Thereafter gross revenue compounds at the through-cycle 3-4.5%, and the adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 11.0% as the $50m technology restructuring savings offset yield normalisation. Owner FCF margin on gross revenue ~7%, in line with the FY2023-25 average of 7.4%. Terminal value is capped at 17x owner FCF (Gordon at 9%/3% would be 17.2x), consistent with a mature, high-ROIC but rate-cyclical forwarder.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-centre hardware becomes a durable, growing airfreight vertical uncorrelated with retail cycles; the tariff regime keeps proliferating (Section 301/232, IEEPA) so customs brokerage -- already 39% of revenue and growing double digits -- keeps compounding at the highest margin in the mix; CEO Wall's market-share gains persist and the technology restructuring plus AI productivity in customs processing lift the adjusted EBITDA margin to 12% (its FY2016-21 range). Growth 6% in years 3-4 fading to 3.5%; terminal cap 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Both episodic drivers reverse together: hyperscaler capex digests, freighter capacity catches up and airfreight rates fall (year 2 -12%, the FY2023-style unwind); a US-China de-escalation or accelerated sourcing diversification away from the China/Hong Kong lanes (~19% of revenue) removes the customs surge; a trade slowdown compresses volumes and yields simultaneously. Margin troughs at 9.6% (below the FY2008-09 ~9%-9.5% GAAP trough only marginally, because customs mix is richer now) and recovers only to 10.3%. Cap 15x, terminal growth 2.5%. Bear remains solidly cash-generative -- there is no solvency dimension, only a de-rating.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the through-cycle owner FCF of an asset-light forwarder, not the current print. Revenue and yield are set by freight rates the company does not control, so the model normalises the 2026 AI-airfreight and tariff-customs spike in year 2 and capitalises a mature 11% adjusted EBITDA margin at a capped multiple. Buybacks are the mechanism that holds the count flat and are not credited as growth; the net-cash pile is added once and its interest stripped from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Freight-rate cycle: gross revenue swung 17.1bn (FY2022) to 9.3bn (FY2023); the year-2 normalisation could be deeper (bear -12%) or not arrive at all (bull)
Durability of AI-hyperscaler airfreight demand -- a new vertical with no cycle history
US tariff regime: complexity drives the highest-margin customs line up, but volume destruction or a de-escalation drives it down; ~19% of revenue on China/Hong Kong export lanes
Non-asset model has no structural cost advantage versus Kuehne+Nagel, DSV, DHL; digital forwarders and direct carrier relationships are a disintermediation risk
Buybacks at ~29x owner FCF (Q2-2026 average $148.87, price now 187) transfer value from continuing holders if the intrinsic value here is right
Terminal value is capped (17x) rather than Gordon; a market that keeps paying 25x+ earnings for EXPD will disagree with this model indefinitely

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 112.95-194.59; regular-session close, not after-hours
data_sources.financials: EXPD_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL companyfacts, CIK 0000746515) for FY2007-Q2 2026; SEC companyfacts pulled 2026-09-28 for cover-page shares (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 2026-07-31), diluted/basic weighted shares, operating lease liabilities, AR/AP/accrued/deferred revenue, pre-tax income, income taxes paid, NCI at 2026-06-30
data_sources.qualitative: EXPD_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): business model, segment mix (customs 39% / air 36% / ocean 25%), Q2-2026 results, FY2026 capex guidance ~$80m, $50m Global Technology restructuring savings, bull/bear points

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow statement, TTM to 2026-06-30: ShareBasedCompensation 75.4 (FY2025 69.2 - H1-25 38.8 + H1-26 45.0) plus cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement 21.5 (no combined figure is published, so the two lines are summed)
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-06-30 financing-activity repurchases (FY2025 667.3 - H1-25 408.5 + H1-26 642.5). The flat count is funded: EXPD retires ~1.5-2m shares a quarter, which is how SBC dilution is neutralised in practice. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model; the cash is already charged as SBC.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page count 129,990,622 at 2026-07-31 (Q2-2026 10-Q) plus 0.42m dilutive awards (Q2-2026 diluted 131.372m less basic 130.953m) = 130.4m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (expensing and diluting would double-charge). No non-SBC issuance.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 less H1-2025 plus H1-2026), so the flows end on the same date as the balance sheet used for net cash and the share count. Year 1 is the twelve months to June 2027. Using FY2025 as FY0 with the June-2026 balance sheet would count H1-2026 cash twice (once as year-1 FCF, once as the shares it already retired).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z regular close (Friday); Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.95 = ~9.0% cost of equity; no borrowings, so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Cyclicality is charged through the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight, not through a WACC premium, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842; liability $567m at 2026-06-30, cost $146m in FY2025) are charged INSIDE EBITDA as US GAAP operating lease cost, so they stay in the flows and lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is $2.4m at 2026-06-30 (0.1% of equity) -- immaterial, no deduction.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax rate anchored to FY2025 taxes paid 265.0 / pre-tax 1,094.1 = 24.2% and the GAAP rate 25.8% (H1-2026 GAAP 25.2%). 25.5% used in base -- slightly above cash because the model taxes EBIT ex interest income and EXPD has no structural shelters; FY2023's 35% cash rate was FY2022 timing, not a run-rate.
inputs.working_capital_note: AR 2,631 vs AP 1,468, accrued 608 and deferred revenue 349 at 2026-06-30: net operating WC ~1.7% of TTM revenue on the full definition, ~9.7% on AR-less-AP. Growth consumes cash (a forwarder pays carriers before customers pay it), so wc_capture is negative at -4% of the YoY revenue change.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing row: operating company, cyclical). Expeditors is a non-asset freight forwarder and customs broker; its value is the stream of owner FCF on the net-revenue spread, so the standard engine applies. No prior DCF or memory entry -- fresh build. The adaptations file was not needed: USD filer, USD quote, leases inside EBITDA, NCI immaterial, SBC disclosed. Interest income (32.8 TTM) is stripped from the FCF base because net cash 1,031 exceeds the owner-FCF base -- the pile is added once in the bridge. TTM owner FCF of 794 is a cyclical high: revenue grew 32% in Q2-2026 on AI-hyperscaler airfreight and tariff-driven customs work that management itself calls partly temporary, which is why the base path has a year-2 normalisation dip and why the bear weight is above the house default. EBITDA margin path is ADJUSTED (pre-SBC) EBITDA on gross revenue; the engine then charges SBC as its own line. Market price 187.46 implies ~24.4bn market cap and ~29x TTM owner FCF, versus a 10-year average adjusted EBITDA margin of ~11.4% and 5.3% revenue CAGR.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (TTM Jun-27 vs TTM Jun-26) +10%: H2-2026 keeps the Q2 run-rate (~3.4bn/qtr) on AI-hyperscaler airfreight and elevated customs work, H1-2027 softens. Year 2 -3%: airfreight rates and tariff-driven brokerage surge normalise. Years 3-10 4.5% fading to 3%: through-cycle gross-revenue growth between the 5yr (2.9%) and 10yr (5.3%) CAGRs.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin on gross revenue: TTM 10.9% (incl. 25m restructuring charge), FY2025 10.6%, FY2024 11.0%, FY2023 11.5%, 10yr average ~11.4%. Base holds 11.0% at maturity: the $50m Global Technology savings (~0.4pp) offsets yield normalisation as the episodic tailwinds fade.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex guidance ~$80m on ~13bn revenue = 0.6%; historical 0.4-0.6%. D&A 0.5% (FY2025 0.51%). Capex held marginally above D&A at maturity.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the FCF base is a cyclical high built on two tailwinds management itself flags as partly temporary, and the price already sits at a 52-week high. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: durable AI airfreight, a persistently complex tariff regime, and margin expansion to 12%. No solvency risk in any path, so the bear is a de-rating, not an impairment.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
